# 別本周易本義

**Custom ID:** ZB1a0031

## Authors / Editors
- 朱熹 (宋朝) 撰 1130 - 1200
- 成矩 (明朝) 編

**Editions:** WYG

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The post-Yǒnglè condensed four-juan recension of Zhū Xī's *Zhōuyì běnyì*, registered as a parallel companion to the original twelve-juan recension [KR1a0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0031). Where [KR1a0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0031) preserves Zhū Xī's authorial juan-arrangement (upper-and-lower canon as 2 juan + Ten Wings as 10 juan = 12 juan), the present *Bié běn* follows the post-Yǒnglè *dà quán*-mediated structure that conjoined Zhū's commentary with [程頤](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%A8%8B%E9%A0%A4) Chéng Yí's [KR1a0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0016) hexagram-and-line ordering, then extracted Zhū's *Běnyì* alone — but with Chéng's juan-divisions retained, scrambling Zhū's *yuán běn* into a 4-juan form. The Míng compiler-and-editor [成矩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%88%90%E7%9F%A9) Chéng Jǔ stabilized this rearranged form for circulation.

The Sìkù *tiyao* on this *Bié běn* uses verbatim the same tiyao text as the *Yuán běn* [KR1a0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0031) (with a small textual slip stating "twelve juan" rather than four — the editors' copy-paste from the parallel registration); the entire scholarly substance of the entry is therefore the same. The Sìkù registration of the two recensions side by side is the editors' programmatic statement: the *Yuán běn* [KR1a0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0031) is the textually authoritative form (the Wú Gé 1265 print with its preserved authorial structure), but the *Bié běn* (the Yǒnglè-mediated 4-juan form, here in Chéng Jǔ's redaction) is the form actually current in late-Míng and Qīng pedagogy. Both must be in the imperial library: the textually-correct one for scholars, the historically-current one for the examination tradition.

For full philological-and-doctrinal exposition, see [KR1a0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0031) *Yuán běn Zhōuyì běnyì*. For the textual-corruption history that produced this *Bié běn*, see [顧炎武](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A1%A7%E7%82%8E%E6%AD%A6) Gù Yánwǔ's *Rì zhī lù* analysis, summarized in the *tiyao* on [KR1a0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0031).

The composition span 1175–1450 covers the entire period from the original *Běnyì*'s composition to Chéng Jǔ's mid-Míng editorial fixing of the *Bié běn* form. The doctrinal core is Zhū Xī's 1175–1188; the redactional layer is Yǒnglè-and-after.

**Abstract**

The *Bié běn Zhōuyì běnyì* is the formally-distinct Sìkù registration of Zhū Xī's *Běnyì* in its post-Yǒnglè condensed-and-rearranged four-juan form, edited under the Míng editor [成矩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%88%90%E7%9F%A9) Chéng Jǔ. The doctrinal substance is Zhū Xī's; the redactional history (the [董楷](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%91%A3%E6%A5%B7) Dǒng Kǎi → Yǒnglè *dà quán* → commercial conflation → Chéng Jǔ's 4-juan extraction) is documented in detail in the *tiyao* on [KR1a0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0031).

The Sìkù editors' decision to register two parallel forms of the *Běnyì* (the *Yuán běn* and the *Bié běn*) reflects their dual loyalty: textual-philological correctness (which favors the *Yuán běn*) and historical-pedagogical fact (which acknowledges that the *Bié běn* is the form actually used in Yuán–Míng–Qīng *Yì* pedagogy). The pattern is unique within the *Yì*-section: no other commentary receives this dual-registration treatment.

[成矩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%88%90%E7%9F%A9) Chéng Jǔ is otherwise undocumented (CBDB has only the bare entry). His role in fixing the four-juan recension is significant — he is the principal Míng-period editor who stabilized the post-Yǒnglè form — but his biographical context is not recoverable from current sources.

The textual problem the Sìkù editors document at length on [KR1a0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0031) applies *especially* to the *Bié běn*: it is the *Bié běn* that exhibits the corruptions Gù Yánwǔ catalogued (the lost juan-headers, the inserted *Tuàn yuē* / *Xiàng yuē* / *Wényán yuē* markers, the deleted "*cóng Wáng Sù běn*" attribution, the Záguà *gǎn sù / cháng jiǔ* → *sù / jiǔ* abbreviation, the dropped Chéng-citation markers replaced by inserted Chéng-text). Reading the *Bié běn* against the *Yuán běn* is the textual-philological exercise the Sìkù editors implicitly recommend.
